problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 34 units, revenue 42 credits
* Container 2: weight 43 units, revenue 225 credits
* Container 3: weight 43 units, revenue 66 credits
* Container 4: weight 37 units, revenue 225 credits
* Container 5: weight 30 units, revenue 47 credits
* Container 6: weight 48 units, revenue 61 credits
* Container 7: weight 47 units, revenue 243 credits
* Container 8: weight 41 units, revenue 85 credits
* Container 9: weight 25 units, revenue 104 credits
* Container 10: weight 27 units, revenue 297 credits
* Container 11: weight 3 units, revenue 186 credits
* Container 12: weight 28 units, revenue 152 credits
* Container 13: weight 19 units, revenue 82 credits
* Container 14: weight 6 units, revenue 300 credits
* Container 15: weight 29 units, revenue 289 credits
* Container 16: weight 21 units, revenue 106 credits
* Container 17: weight 36 units, revenue 32 credits
* Container 18: weight 15 units, revenue 237 credits
* Container 19: weight 48 units, revenue 269 credits
* Container 20: weight 27 units, revenue 79 credits
* Container 21: weight 36 units, revenue 286 credits
* Container 22: weight 3 units, revenue 110 credits
* Container 23: weight 19 units, revenue 294 credits
* Container 24: weight 14 units, revenue 145 credits
* Container 25: weight 4 units, revenue 272 credits

The vehicle has a maximum weight capacity of 478 units. Determine which containers to load to maximize total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
